text: 43 tolde 23 and 36 in great earnest that discovering of
mindes and goodwilles to 93 wch was odious to 94. and some
soch, had vndone them all and truly 36 is of opinion that some soch
thing hath made 93 so mad as it appeareth wth 23. that he
will not heare him what ever 70 can doe, yet Feria promiseth vppon
94 and 95 retorne that some thing shalbe done.
40. 24. 23. 42. and some others have delt so long with one Captayn
White of Flushing that he is of late hanged for treason.
A marchant of ? for lodging one Captayn White and being suspected of
societye wth him is banished for 50. yeares all his goodes confiscate and
he come hither wth wife and children in miserye being a very riche man
before.
Mr Tipping wth his wife and children are come hither from St Omers. et
vadet habitatũ Mecliniam. Our regiment hath now no
Commaunder and being appoynted by the Count to lye in ? Clow
because they have no paye they ravage the Countrye at wch the Count
rageth and hath sent for the Coronell abowt it threatning to hange
the soldiors or to Cashe the Regiment.
Ligons is of opinion that 40. his make theyr vantage of
nothing so moch agaynst 20 as of 20 his frendes favor to
73. Sciam in 102 scibas si 72. sit absolvendus
Vxor 73 pro certissimo est reconciliata sed id est valde secretum
tamen 113. dixit pro compertissimo 23.
Some advises are come that Mr Moore and Williamson were sent over of
purpose to doe mischefe. Eventus probabit nemini tamen puto eos posse
nocere.
43. telle me that he had advertisment from Spayne that 35.
being in 105. and 36 wth theis 82. did nothing content
25. 26. 24. 40. etc. and that 26. 25. and his lay in wayte to
discredit 36 and 22. being wth 2 nephew will as
litle please ?? Englished.
Of Nicholas Williamsons imprisonment in the Towre of London of the likelywood
of execution of father Walpoole, F. Edmondes, Mr Sowlond, of the going owt of
the orange agaynst the xxij. of Aprill, of an oath to be ministred to all the
subjects of the realme vt sint fideles contra ? invasionem, Mr Paget
will write quicquid sit. that mans talking hath moch trobled my Lord ?
departure not knowing how to depart or to go forward in his pasport and
and enterprise of Scotland and now (as his sonne told 36. is resolved to
goe (quia cum honore non potest manere) sed alia via.
Yours wth all the inclosed are safe arrived wch you wrate the 22. of Aprill and
wee received the 14. of May.
The D. d’Aumale was receaved here this day wth greate honor the Count Fuentes
being on his right hand and the Duke de Feria (almost madde wth melancholye,
moch 93 hath written agaynst him to Spayne to disable him for this
government) on his left. He pretendeth to come a begging partlye for
dewes for forage given to our Campe partly for some benevolence, yet the
Spanyardes wold make men beleve that he cometh wth some great enterprise
quasi vero cum nec habeat Civitatem nec Castellum quod vendat nec militem
vel sequaces quorum opera vtatur. xv. Maij.
16. hath talked long wth me and vttered soch matter
agaynst 20. that 36 easelye may perceave that he hath bene
instructed in the scole of 31. 32. and 40. yet I salved him
merelye well. He sayd inter alia that yong Tempeste there was deboshed
by Signor Hugo, and had deboshed the Scollers wch yow tooke so muche agaynst
him 28. so putt him owt, that 20. shamefully had sowght the
voyces of 29. ut loqueretur in persona aliorum and before he departed
I made him protest another matter.
I thinke 23. accusing to 93 will prove Brownes doing 24.
for sweareth it although he invaye infinitelye agaynst 42. and wold
fayne have 23. renownce him vt libere in eum posset sævire
although I thinke truly 42. hath done 23 more harme
then good.
82. is angry first that 24. 113. 147. et alij give out
that 90. was offred to 73. who demaunding whether there were
any men arrived and vnderstanding quod non, refused 90. wch 82.
telleth 36. in secrett is a flatt lye, but to the Ende
pagador shold know nothing, 90. being gotten out of
his handes he was sent to Catnesse into the North. Quicquid sit
82. iurat se nunquam cum 83. habiturum rem etiam si
2. imperet. My Nuncio told 36. for assured that Perone
was not yet departed towardes 105. and that 2. was madde
wth 82. for those letters and if 72. proceded not in the
demaund of absolution that all wold be imputed to 82. letters
